# Extraction template spec (Covidence review 818465)

A literal record of every field and domain configured in Covidence's **Data Extraction** and
**Quality Assessment** templates, built and published 15 Oct 2026. Not generated by a script —
built by hand in Covidence's own template editor via browser automation — so this file is the
thing that makes the build reconstructable (or auditable against `protocol.md`) without
re-deriving it from conversation history. If the template is ever rebuilt from scratch, this
is the checklist to type back in.

Template type: **Extraction 1** ("Collecting numerical results across groups"), not
Extraction 2 ("Mapping and describing the evidence") — chosen because the review has a defined
comparator structure (breastfed vs. formula-fed vs. mixed/combination feeding) in every
included study, even though the review's own synthesis is narrative/vote-counting rather than
meta-analytic. See the "Extraction stage" section of this project's `CLAUDE.md` for the
reasoning in full.

The companion human-readable reference — field-by-field instructions, not just field names —
is `Infant_Microbiome_Codebook.docx` (also published as an artifact; see this repo's main
README). This file is the machine-checkable field *list*; the codebook is the *instructions*.

---

## Data Extraction Template

### 1. Identification

Unchanged from Covidence's defaults (Sponsorship source, Country, Setting, Comments; Author's
contact details; Additional data: Start date, End date, Trial registration number). No custom
fields — Section A of the codebook (study ID, country, design, funding) maps onto this and the
Methods section below without needing anything extra here.

### 2. Methods

| Field | Type | Options / notes |
|---|---|---|
| Study design *(built-in, left checked)* | dropdown (fixed, not editable) | Covidence's own list: Randomised controlled trial, Case-control study, Cluster randomised controlled trial, Controlled interrupted time series, Historically controlled trial, Prospective cohort study, Retrospective cohort study, Other. Kept for free PRISMA-style categorization — **not** the field that governs the RoB tool branch (see below). |
| Study design — review classification, governs RoB tool *(custom)* | text (controlled vocabulary in the label) | `RCT / non-randomized intervention / prospective cohort / retrospective cohort / cross-sectional / case-control` — this is the field that decides RoB 2 vs. ROBINS-I at quality-assessment time. Added because the built-in field above has no cross-sectional option and can't be edited. |
| Sequencing method *(custom)* | text | `16S rRNA / shotgun metagenomics / both` |
| 16S hypervariable region *(custom)* | text | e.g. "V3–V4"; write N/A if shotgun-only |
| Sequencing platform *(custom)* | text | e.g. Illumina MiSeq, NovaSeq, Ion PGM |
| Bioinformatic pipeline + version *(custom)* | text | e.g. QIIME2/DADA2, Mothur |
| Reference database + version *(custom)* | text | e.g. SILVA 138, Greengenes, RDP |

### 3. Population

| Field | Type | Options / notes |
|---|---|---|
| Inclusion criteria / Exclusion criteria / Group differences *(built-in, left checked)* | text | Covidence defaults |
| Total sample size / Number of withdrawals / Reason for withdrawals *(built-in, left checked)* | text | Covidence defaults |
| Gestational age range / criteria *(custom)* | text | e.g. "≥37 weeks" |
| Infant age(s) at stool sampling *(custom)* | text | List every timepoint reported, not just baseline |
| Delivery mode reported? *(custom)* | text | Vaginal vs. cesarean Ns if yes |
| Age-stratified results? *(custom)* | text | Fixed bands: 0–1, 1–3, 3–6, 6–12 mo |
| Covariates adjusted for *(custom)* | text (controlled vocabulary in the label) | `delivery mode / antibiotic exposure / introduction of solids / geography / country income level / maternal factors / none` |
| Adequacy of covariate measurement *(custom)* | text | Short note, not a score |
| (a) Race/ethnicity/ancestry — categories as reported *(custom)* | text, **verbatim** | Source's own labels exactly as printed |
| (b) Race/ethnicity/ancestry — construct used *(custom)* | text | `race / ethnicity / ancestry / combined-or-conflated / NOT REPORTED` |
| (c) Race/ethnicity/ancestry — ascertainment *(custom)* | text | `self-report / investigator-assigned / administrative-registry / genetic ancestry markers / NOT REPORTED` |
| (d) Race/ethnicity/ancestry — analytic role *(custom)* | text | `descriptive only / adjusted covariate / stratification variable / not used / NOT REPORTED` |
| Baseline characteristic: Age at stool sampling (months), mean ± SD or range *(repurposed)* | per-group numeric | Was "Mean age (years) ± SD" — relabeled so extractors record age-at-sampling-in-months per feeding group, not enrollment age |

**Note on implementation:** Covidence's "Additional data" fields in Methods/Population are
plain free-text boxes — there is no native dropdown/checkbox type at this level. Controlled
vocabularies above are embedded directly in the field label text; the codebook document is
what actually enforces them at extraction time.

### 4. Interventions

| Group | Notes |
|---|---|
| Breastfed | |
| Formula-fed | |
| Mixed / combination feeding | Only used if a study reports it as its own group — per the settled scope, not a default third arm |

Per-group detail fields (replacing Covidence's drug-trial defaults of Dose/Frequency, which
don't apply to a feeding exposure):

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| Number of participants allocated *(kept)* | |
| Verbatim feeding-group definition *(replaces Dose)* | Exact quote from the study, not a paraphrase |
| Classification *(replaces Frequency)* | `exclusive / predominant / any / mixed-as-distinct-group / other` |
| Ascertainment *(added)* | `prospective record / caregiver recall / not stated` |

### 5. Outcomes

All 9 outcomes set to Covidence's **Qualitative** result-data type (not Continuous or
Dichotomous) — the review synthesizes narratively by vote-counting direction of effect, not by
pooling numeric effect sizes, so the continuous/dichotomous result-table columns (mean/SD/
total, events/total) don't apply.

1. Alpha diversity
2. Beta diversity
3. Bifidobacterium (relative abundance)
4. Bacteroides (relative abundance)
5. Clostridia (relative abundance)
6. Enterobacteriaceae (relative abundance)
7. Lactobacillus (relative abundance)
8. Other differentially abundant taxa
9. Functional outcomes

Not yet configured: the per-outcome result-table columns (e.g. a custom "Direction of effect"
column carrying the review's four-way scale — higher in breastfed / higher in formula-fed / no
difference / not estimable). Covidence supports custom result-table columns per outcome; this
wasn't built out in the 15 Oct session and is worth doing before extraction starts at volume.

## Quality Assessment Template

Custom template (not the Cochrane RoB1 preset Covidence offers by default — neither RoB 2 nor
ROBINS-I is available as a built-in choice). 17 domains, each carrying its own correct
judgement scale (Covidence's custom-domain editor supports this per-domain, not just
template-wide).

### RoB 2 (RCTs only) — 5 domains, scale: Low / Some concerns / High

1. Randomization process
2. Deviations from intended interventions
3. Missing outcome data
4. Measurement of the outcome
5. Selection of the reported result

### ROBINS-I (observational only) — 7 domains, scale: Low / Moderate / Serious / Critical / No information

1. Confounding
2. Selection of participants
3. Classification of exposures
4. Deviations from intended exposures
5. Missing data
6. Measurement of outcomes
7. Selection of the reported result

### Checklist (every study, regardless of design) — 5 domains, scale: Yes / No / Not reported

1. Sample collection and storage method reported
2. DNA extraction method reported
3. Sequencing depth reported
4. Negative/positive contamination controls reported
5. Compositional-data handling reported

This checklist isn't a convenience add-on — `protocol.md`'s Risk of bias paragraph specifies
it directly ("Supplemented by a microbiome-specific methods checklist..."), assessed with the
same dual-reviewer-plus-adjudication rigor as RoB 2/ROBINS-I, and it was added to close a gap
the live PROSPERO record (CRD420261485879) already claimed was covered.

No Outcome groups were configured — none of the 17 domains are scoped to individual outcome
groups ("Can apply to individual outcome groups?" left unchecked on all of them), since RoB
2/ROBINS-I here assess the study/comparison as a whole, not a specific named outcome.

## Known issues / gotchas found building this

### 1. "Additional data" fields don't auto-save — nothing persists until Publish is clicked

**Symptom:** after building out Methods, Population, Interventions, and Outcomes in one
sitting, attempting to navigate away triggered a browser "Leave site?" unsaved-changes
warning. Opening the same template fresh in a second tab (a genuine server round-trip, not
cached state) showed Methods/Population's custom fields reverted to empty and
Interventions/Outcomes reverted to "Set Up" (unconfigured) — none of it had actually reached
the server.

**Root cause:** Covidence's template editor holds field-level edits in client-side state only;
there is no per-field autosave on blur, contrary to how most inline-editable UIs behave.
**Publish template** is the only commit action for the template *structure* itself (distinct
from per-study extraction data, which does autosave).

**The fix:** click Publish template to commit, confirmed via the same fresh-tab check
afterward (all fields present, "Published less than a minute ago by Philip" shown). Worth
remembering for any future template edit: changes sit in memory, unprotected, until published.

### 2. The built-in "Study design" field is fixed, not editable, and has no cross-sectional option

**Symptom:** planned to edit Covidence's default Study design dropdown to the review's own six
design categories (including cross-sectional, needed for the RoB-tool branch decision).
Clicking its info icon opened a static list, not an editable options editor.

**Root cause:** the built-in Study design field in Extraction 1's Methods section is a fixed
system field — its option list (Randomised controlled trial / Case-control study / Cluster
RCT / Controlled interrupted time series / Historically controlled trial / Prospective cohort
study / Retrospective cohort study / Other) is not configurable, and it has no cross-sectional
option at all.

**The fix:** added a separate custom field, "Study design — review classification, governs RoB
tool," carrying the review's own exact six categories, and left the built-in field checked but
not authoritative. Documented in both this spec and the codebook so extractors know which
field actually decides the RoB 2/ROBINS-I branch.

## What's not here

No PDFs, no extracted data, no actual RoB/checklist judgements — this stage is template
*setup* only. 111 included studies are ready for extraction; 0 extracted as of 15 Oct 2026.
